Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines — defense routing / evidence staging

David — thanks for taking this. Attached are our proposed redlines to the MSA and Order Form focusing on the defense/indemnity sections. High level background: we are evaluating Redwood for a clinical insights pilot; legal is asking for clarity on how an IP infringement notice would be routed and who bears evidence collection costs where model output is implicated.

Two immediate asks from our side:
- Can Redwood confirm whether you will accept "right to defend" for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs, and if so, how you propose to sequence insurance contribution -> escrow -> customer reimbursement?
- We need an operations-level evidence staging plan: who will be the technical custodian for logs/artifacts, SLA for producing an evidence bundle, and a secure delivery mechanism for potentially privileged materials.

I flagged a few clauses in meditech_proposed_redlines.docx (attached). We can be flexible on allocation if we have firm commitments on evidence turn-around (we cannot wait multiple weeks for raw logs in a live incident).

Would you and your legal lead (cc'd below) be available for a 30-min alignment call tomorrow? If you have alternate language you prefer, please paste it in-line in a reply so we can iterate quickly.

Thanks,
Sasha Kov
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
MediTech Systems
[Attachment: meditech_proposed_redlines.docx (DOCX)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sasha Kov <sasha.kov@meditech.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 16:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines — defense routing / evidence staging

Sasha — appreciate the detailed redlines and the fast turnaround. Quick replies to your two asks and a proposed path forward:

1) Right to defend: Redwood is generally willing to accept right to defend for third-party IP claims tied to model outputs, subject to carveouts for customer-supplied content and modifications. We prefer to keep the primary right to defend (to preserve consistency in defense strategy), but we can include a commitment to consult and coordinate with Meditech on technical evidence collection.

2) Insurance/escrow sequencing: proposed waterfall (summary):
   - Primary insurer contribution (Redwood's CGL/IP policy) up to policy limits
   - If insurer shortfall: Redwood to cover defense costs up to an agreed cap (we propose $250k for pilots)
   - Beyond that, consider escrow or cost-sharing tied to quantifiable usage metrics (we can define a token-based metric)

3) Evidence staging and custody:
   - Tech custodian: Redwood infra team will assemble a time-sliced evidence bundle (requesting a 72-hour SLA for initial package and 7 days for deeper artifacts).
   - Delivery: secure SFTP or a shared, encrypted Drive link (we've included a proposed folder in related_links).
   - Privilege: anything flagged as privileged by either party can be handled via separate counsel-to-counsel transfer; we will avoid over-sharing until privilege is sorted.

Kimberly, I've pasted a short redline below that narrows the scope and adds staging SLAs; happy to iterate:

--- suggested insertion for Order Form / Annex X (draft language) ---
"For third-party claims alleging that Customer Data or Customer-provided model artifacts infringe a third party's intellectual property, Redwood shall have the right, at its election, to assume sole control of the defense and settlement of such Claim; provided, however, that Redwood shall (i) promptly notify Customer of any such Claim, (ii) consult with Customer regarding defense strategy, and (iii) produce an initial evidence bundle described in Annex X within seventy-two (72) hours of receipt of a materially complete written notice. If Redwood's insurer contribution is insufficient to cover defense costs, Redwood will cover defense costs up to two hundred fifty thousand U.S. dollars (USD 250,000) for pilot engagements; any amounts above this cap shall be split pro rata based on agreed usage metrics unless otherwise agreed in writing."

--- end insertion ---

Operational ask for the call: can you confirm whether Meditech can accept 72/168 (hours) SLA windows for initial / full evidence delivery? Also, can you identify the internal Meditech tech contact who will receive the evidence bundle?

Ben will set up the call if we get a yes on the times.

Best,
David
Head of Legal Partnerships (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
[Attachment: sla-timeline.pdf (PDF)]

David / Sasha — quick substantive comments from legal:

- Scope tightening: recommend a narrow definition for claims "arising solely from model outputs generated by Redwood's hosted runtime absent Customer-provided prompts or content." This reduces exposure for Ruby/Redwood where customer prompt engineering or post-processing introduces liability.

- Evidence SLA: 72/168 is aggressive but acceptable for pilots if we include a cooperating clause that requires Customer to provide reasonably requested context within 24 hours of Redwood's initial evidence request. Without that cooperation, SLA obligations should be tolled.

- Insurance cap and carveouts: instead of a fixed cap in the main order form, propose the cap be set in the Order Form as a negotiated pilot parameter (e.g., OrderForm Exhibit A) — that gives sales procurement flexibility.

- Suggested redline to add privilege protection and limited disclosure: insert clause requiring counsel-to-counsel transfer for materials marked "privileged" and a carveout allowing Redwood to redact PII and internal operator logs where disclosure would create security risk.

I pasted a short redline snippet below you can paste into Meditech's doc:

--- Kimberly's redline snippet ---
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer acknowledges that Redwood's defense obligations do not extend to Claims arising from (a) Customer-provided data, prompts, or model artifacts; (b) Customer modifications to Redwood's runtime or models; or (c) Customer's failure to timely cooperate in the collection of technical evidence. Redwood's obligation to deliver an evidence bundle is conditioned on Customer's timely cooperation as reasonably requested by Redwood. Materials asserted as privileged by either party shall be transferred counsel-to-counsel and excluded from non-privileged evidence production; Redwood may redact sensitive operational telemetry to the extent necessary for security and confidentiality."

--- end snippet ---

Ben — for procurement, please propose a pilot-specific cap value (David's $250k is a starting point) and confirm whether we can make the cap a line-item on the Order Form. Also confirm who in sales will sign off on the Exhibit A for pilots.

Sasha — if Meditech can confirm the tech contact and cooperation commitment we will prepare a clean counter-redline and route for call.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
